chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man was asked: He has wealth due from another man on credit, which he had specified for him. When the payment became due, the debtor did not have what to give him. So he wanted to turn it over for him and profit from it: should he sell him pearls and other things worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, and delay the payment? He said: There is no problem with that. My father did that, may Allah be pleased with him, and he ordered me to do that with regard to anything that was due to him.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to Ibrahim ibn al-Harith or Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, depending on the specific lineage context in al-Kafi)
key_terms.عِينَة: Credit sale or deferred payment transaction
key_terms.لُؤْلُؤاً: Pearls (used here as an example of valuable goods)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods on credit at a higher price to recover a debt when the debtor cannot pay immediately?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi validates the practice of 'in'ah' (or 'tadlil'), where a creditor sells a debt for a higher price on credit to recover funds when the debtor is insolvent. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms its permissibility by citing the precedent of his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), establishing a practical legal mechanism for debt recovery in early Shia jurisprudence.
